en.title: GTA 6 Devs Face Historic Union Vote Amidst Legal Battles
en.summary: Workers at Rockstar Games, the studio behind the highly anticipated **Grand Theft Auto 6**, are on the cusp of a historic decision regarding unionization. The outcome could reshape labor relations within the UK's video game industry.
en.body:
The development of **Grand Theft Auto 6**, a title poised to be one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time, is unfolding alongside a potentially landmark event for its creators. Employees at **Rockstar Games** in the UK are set to participate in a union recognition vote for the **IWGB Union at Rockstar**. This vote, scheduled from November 12th to November 26th, directly overlaps with the highly anticipated launch of **GTA 6** on November 19th, adding an extra layer of drama to an already charged period for the studio.

The **IWGB Union at Rockstar** has been in negotiations with **Rockstar** management for months, aiming to secure a stronger voice for developers on critical issues such as pay, overtime, generative AI policies, remote work arrangements, and layoff procedures. If recognized, this union would represent the largest contingent of video game workers in the UK, marking a significant shift in the industry's labor landscape.

## A Crucial Moment for Game Workers

This unionization drive is not without its challenges and controversies. Coinciding with the vote is the nearing conclusion of an employment tribunal concerning claims that **Rockstar** terminated developers for their union organizing activities. Final arguments in this tribunal are scheduled for November 17th and 18th. The union alleges that over 30 **IWGB** members were dismissed in October 2025 specifically because of their involvement in forming a union. **Rockstar**, however, maintains that these staff members were let go due to leaking confidential information about upcoming games.

The **IWGB** views the situation at **Rockstar North**, the primary developer of **GTA 6**, as particularly significant. Given the immense profile of the **Grand Theft Auto** franchise and the expected global success of **GTA 6**, a successful unionization effort here could inspire and facilitate wider unionization movements across the entire UK gaming sector. As **Rockstar** publishing boss **Jennifer Kolbe** recently stated, "We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union." This statement suggests a willingness from the company's leadership to acknowledge the workers' wishes, though the tribunal proceedings cast a shadow over the relationship.

## What This Means for the Future

For passionate fans eagerly awaiting **Grand Theft Auto 6**, this labor situation adds a complex, human dimension to the creation of their most-anticipated game. The potential for improved working conditions and greater worker protections at a studio known for its demanding production cycles could set a precedent for the entire industry. The **IWGB** committee member **Shanti Easton-Steel** emphasized the historic opportunity, stating that the studio has "the chance to making gaming history" through this vote and the ongoing tribunal.

## What's Next

The union recognition vote runs from November 12th to November 26th, with the **GTA 6** release on November 19th falling squarely within this period. The employment tribunal's final arguments will be heard on November 17th and 18th, potentially delivering crucial context as workers cast their ballots.

content_raw: Workers at GTA 6 developer Rockstar will soon get to vote on recognizing a union. The union, IWGB Union at Rockstar, is for Rockstar's UK-based developers. Rockstar North, based in Edinburgh, Scotland, is one of Rockstar's biggest outfits in the UK, and the lead developer on GTA 6. The negotiating process between the union and Rockstar management took months, and the union, if recognized, would give workers a stronger seat at the table for key issues like pay and bonuses, overtime, generative AI policies, work-from-home setups, and situations involving layoffs. The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the largest in the UK video game sector, if it's voted in. The voting period--November 12-26--overlaps with the release of GTA 6 on November 19. At the same time, an employment tribunal over claims that Rockstar fired developers for trying to form a union is coming to a close, with final arguments set for November 17 and November 18. More than 30 IWGB members were let go from Rockstar in the UK in October 2025, with the union saying Rockstar fired them for trying to form a union . Rockstar, for its part, said the staffers were dismissed for leaking key details about Rockstar's upcoming games. IWGB said the Rockstar case for unionization is an especially important one in the UK because the profile of Rockstar North--the developer of what is expected to be the biggest game of all time--could lead to a more widespread unionization push across gaming. Rockstar publishing boss Jennifer Kolbe told Bloomberg recently, "We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union.” Rockstar Game Workers Union Committee member Shanti Easton-Steel said the studio has "the chance to making gaming history" with the upcoming unionization vote and the tribunal decision. "As all our hard work, skill and creativity are experienced by GTA 6 players for the first time, our voices will now be heard for the first time too," Easton-Steel said. "When management choices are kept hidden, we can’t properly address issues like the gender pay gap, the uneven and ever-changing policies on overtime pay, or the concerns many co-workers hold around job security post-release." IWGB Union president Alex Marshall added, "For anyone who cares about the games industry or the people who keep it running, this vote is just as historic as the game release. But for workers at Rockstar, it is so much more personal: it is fundamentally a choice about whether you get to have a say in how your day-to-day life is organized." While the movie industry in Hollywood and beyond are largely unionized, the same is not true for video games. Unions are far more rare, but that's changing somewhat, as more and more developers in the US and worldwide are unionizing. For example, more than 1,900 workers at Blizzard recently reached a unionization contract with Microsoft , with workers winning things like guaranteed raises, guardrails on AI, and more.
